newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma in new peace talks with Karen rebels.
newsitem.headline: Burma in new peace talks with Karen rebels.

text.p: Burma's military government said on Saturday that it was awaiting the outcome of a new round of peace talks with ethnic Karen rebel guerrillas operating along the forested southeastern border with Thailand.

Spokesman Colonel Kyaw Thein told a monthly news conference that some influential Karen nationals from Rangoon were now meeting rebel Karen National Union (KNU) leaders to persuade them to make peace with the government.

"Right now some influential Karen people are discussing in detail with the KNU leaders to ask them to come into the legal fold," he said. "They reached the KNU headquarters three days ago. We now have to wait for the outcome."

The KNU was formed in 1948 to fight for autonomy from Rangoon shortly after Burma gained independence from Britain. The KNU is the only remaining armed group still fighting Burma's military government and several rounds of peace talks in the past have failed.

This week the KNU and its rival, the Democratic Karen Buddhist Army (DKBA), a splinter-group backed by the Burmese government, have been engaged in heavy fighting that has left thousands homeless and killed at least three people.
